title: Adaptive paper-MAC memory for bounded E. coli and Escherichia genomic language modeling
scientific_motivation: Test whether a causal genomic language model with adaptive persistent memory improves held-out sequence prediction and predefined region-level diagnostics under matched compute and data controls.

hypotheses.primary: Adaptive memory improves held-out bits per base over matched no-memory and frozen-memory controls at equal data and optimizer budgets.
secondary: Adaptive memory yields useful region-level anomaly detection at a fixed false-positive rate.
The learned memory state contains reproducible information beyond local sequence and GC composition.

scope_limitations: train-only E. coli and Escherichia eligibility

claim_language.supported: improves held-out prediction under the preregistered matched comparison
claim_language.not_supported: functional biological activity or broad Gram-negative generalization

dataset.isolation: validation and test accessions are excluded from fitting and subset selection

tokenizer.name: frozen Stage C tokenizer selected by equal-base CPU gate
tokenizer.normalization: uppercase ACGT with explicit non-ACGT policy

medium.backend: exact accelerated memory with SDPA attention

decision_gates.anomaly: fixed false-positive rate on held-out synthetic and natural regions

confirmatory: anomaly detection at fixed false-positive rate

prohibited_inferences: Generative plausibility is not a functional promoter or gene claim.
The study does not support a broad Gram-negative claim.
No memory-benefit claim without matched controls and second-seed replication.
